purpose: Full A_FR rebuild using the human-approved natural-French-TTS architecture (review/A_FR_natural_voice_test.mp4), replacing the rejected Dubbing v2 (A_FR_v2) approach. Per-segment natural French TTS, adaptive video timing (loop real motion, no forced compression), selective fal.ai lip-sync, French burned captions.
architecture: Existing Gemini French translation (reports/A_FR_translation.json, reused verbatim, no new Gemini calls) -> ElevenLabs native French TTS (per-segment, natural duration) -> adaptive video timing per segment -> fal.ai lip-sync on visible-speaking segments -> burned-in French captions -> concat -> QA.

voice.voice_name: Yann - Warm & Deep Storyteller (fr-FR Voice Library, not a clone of the source speaker)

per_segment_generation.generation_method: One ElevenLabs TTS call per segment (not one call for the whole script), so each segment's natural duration is known individually for per-segment video adaptation and caption timing.

video_adaptation.method_non_lipsync_segments: Original segment footage looped (ffmpeg -stream_loop, real motion repeated, not a static freeze) when natural French audio needed more time than the original English segment; trimmed when shorter. This follows the instructed priority of extending reusable real motion over freeze-holds.
video_adaptation.method_lipsync_segments: fal.ai sync-lipsync v2 pro called with sync_mode='loop': the model itself extends/loops the source video to match the natural French audio duration while generating matching mouth movement, rather than us pre-extending video before lip-sync.

segment_with_largest_extension.note: 3.10s -> 5.06s natural French, a lip-sync segment (fal loop-extended); worth a specific look in review for any looping artifact given the size of the stretch.

lipsync.model: fal-ai/sync-lipsync/v2/pro (same approved model used for the frozen A_DE/A_FR/A_KO v1 builds)
lipsync.segment_selection_rationale: Same lipsync_segment_ids as the already-approved v1 pipeline (onscreen_mouth_speaking_this_line AND visual_content=='creator_talking_head').

21.note: needed 2 retries due to transient network timeouts, not a generation-quality issue; succeeded on 3rd attempt.

lipsync.audio_source_confirmation: Each lip-sync call's audio_url was the segment's own French TTS audio (assets/generated/challenger_A/fr_v3/tts/seg_NN.mp3 -> uploaded aac). fal.ai's response video was re-muxed with -map 1:a from that same fal output (never from original English), so the original English audio cannot have re-entered the mix for these 5 segments.
lipsync.persisted: assets/generated/challenger_A/fr_v3/lipsync/seg_NN_lipsynced.mp4, checkpointed before any local compose step, per idempotency instruction.

captions.text_source: reports/A_FR_translation.json localized_text, unchanged (same wording as A_FR_v2/A_FR.mp4)
captions.timing: Captions are built and burned per-segment onto each segment's own final-duration clip, so caption timing is exact to that segment's actual natural French audio -- no separate STT-based retiming pass was needed (unlike the Dubbing v2 builds, where ElevenLabs' own translation text differed from ours and required STT-anchored retiming).
captions.style: Same font/placement/black-bar style as all prior Challenger A localizations (Arial Black, black bar y=1090-1490, white text with black stroke) -- mobile-safe, does not cover the upper 1090px where UI/payment-proof screenshots appear.
captions.language_check: All 23 caption lines are French text taken directly from the approved translation file; none were regenerated or altered.

CONFIRMED_DEFECT_ENGLISH_LEAKAGE.severity: FAIL -- confirmed, not a heuristic guess
CONFIRMED_DEFECT_ENGLISH_LEAKAGE.summary: The video's tail (originally 50.1s-57.4547s of final/A_EN.mp4, appended UNTRANSLATED/UNCHANGED at the end of A_FR_v3 -- now at ~62.37-69.73s in the new timeline) contains real spoken English: 'All right, I'm getting it' at 62.88-63.92s, immediately after segment 22's correct French line 'C'est bon, je la télécharge' (same meaning). This is genuine English-dialogue leakage AND duplicated/overlapping dialogue (two back-to-back renderings, French then English, of the same line) -- both explicitly-checked QA gates.
CONFIRMED_DEFECT_ENGLISH_LEAKAGE.root_cause: This tail was deliberately left as original/untouched based on a build-time assumption (confirmed via two smaller manual STT spot-checks before the full build) that it was ambient/SFX-only. That assumption was WRONG -- it was checked at 50.1s and 51.0s starts and both returned similar-sounding phrases, which was misread as probable STT hallucination on music rather than genuine trailing dialogue. The full-file STT run after assembly now conclusively shows real English speech there, plus a notification SFX right at the very end.
CONFIRMED_DEFECT_ENGLISH_LEAKAGE.fix_not_yet_applied: Per instruction not to make unrequested changes mid-review, this was NOT patched. Two fix options for a follow-up: (a) translate/TTS+caption this tail line too and append it properly, or (b) trim the video to end at the true last French line (~62.37s) if this tail line is redundant/unwanted in the final ad. Needs a decision from you.

FLAGGED_FOR_LISTENING_REVIEW.finding: STT transcribed this span as 'build to ghost' rather than a recognizable rendering of 'ils te ghostent'. 'Ghoster' as a verb is a French slang/franglais borrowing from English, which may be harder for the TTS model to pronounce naturally in French -- could be a genuine mispronunciation, or an STT quirk on an unusual loanword. Worth a specific listen at ~17s; not counted as English leakage since the underlying text and intent are French, but flagged as a possible pronunciation issue.
